criteria.description: The result is one concise, creator-reviewable 60-second production specification grounded in the supplied screenplay. It does not become a source audit, generic workflow, production diary, or set of separate stage documents.

The specification establishes one coherent plot spine plus source-grounded character goals, scene functions, visual style, action, sound, scope, and acceptance rules that downstream production must preserve.

Generation-critical character, scene and style anchors, keyframes or masks, and storyboard or animatic assets are explicit, source-grounded, have direct acceptance conditions, and are mapped to their consuming units.

One authoritative table gives stable production-unit identity and owns timing, story function, image/action/camera/sound, bound inputs, semantic generation intent, expected asset, direct acceptance, repair boundary, and downstream use without duplicating those decisions elsewhere.

One cross-unit contract gives applicable editorial, compositing, grade, sound, title or caption, review work, clean or stem variants, platform delivery, QC and manifest constraints. Unknown measured or platform-specific parameters remain explicit dependencies rather than invented defaults.

The document contains no raw model call packet because execution was excluded, and it does not copy runtime status, candidate history, failures, project revisions, or export receipts into prose. Source analysis appears only as a compact decision map, not reading narration.
